Zeldin said the change would save $54 billion each year. The search followed the National Archives’ recovery of 15 boxes earlier that year and a May 2022 grand-jury subpoena seeking additional records. Investigators obtained evidence that classified material remained at the property after a sworn statement from Trump’s legal team said a diligent search had been conducted. The episode concerned the handling and retention of government records after Trump left office. title: Thousands of Children Separated From Parents at Border
description_short: Thousands of Children Separated From Parents at Border

A later report found problems tracking separated families.
description_long: In spring 2018, reports made public the scale of family separations under the Trump administration’s “zero tolerance” prosecution policy. More than 2,300 children were separated from parents during May and June, and some were held in crowded facilities that drew criticism after audio and images circulated. The administration signed an executive order on June 20 to halt the practice, but ending new separations did not immediately reunite families already divided. A later inspector-general review found dangerous overcrowding at several facilities, while agencies struggled to maintain records that could reliably match children with parents. The supplied record says hundreds remained separated months or years later. This sequence shows that a policy reversal and family reunification were different tasks, and that the government lacked adequate tracking systems when separations began. The sentence imposed no jail time, probation, or fine, but it did not erase the jury’s conviction. The judge cited the unprecedented circumstances of sentencing a president-elect and the limits of the court’s options after rejecting Trump’s request to dismiss the case.
